full_judgment:
3. The plaint case, in short, was that Narayan Chandra Das transferred 1.60 acres of land including the soil land to the plaintiff and his nephew Dilip Kumar Das by a kabala dated 04.07.1985. The possession of the transferred land was duly handed over to the transferees, namely, the plaintiff and Dilip Kumar Das. The names of the plaintiff and Dilip Kumar Das were duly Mutated in Mutation Case No. 240 Baw/85-86 and separate Khatians were prepared in their names. In the absence of Narayan Chandra Das, defendant Nos. 1-3 created a forged deed of gift on 29.07.1985 through personation showing Narayan Chandra Das as executant in respect of 1.48 acres of land as described in schedule 'Ka to the plaint the said deed of gift was shown to have been executed on 06.04.1985. On coming to know about such forgery the plaintiff instituted a criminal case being Complaint Case No. 9 of 1986 in the Court of Magistrate, Bawfal, Patuakhali against defendant Nos. 1-4. The said criminal case was compromised by defendant Nos. 1-4 by relinquishing their claim over the suit land. Dilip Kumar Das also instituted Criminal Case No. 15 of 1989 against defendant Nos. 1-5, in Which, on 23.02.1996, defendant No. 5 by filing an application stated that he know nothing about any deed of gift. Narayan Chandra Das never executed the alleged deed of gift, rather he on receipt of TK. 50,000.00 from the plaintiff, and his nephew Dilip Kumar Das transferred 1.60 acres of land including the suit land by executing and registering the kabala dated 04.07.1985. After handing over possession of the transferred land, to the plaintiff and Dilip Kumar Das, Narayan Chandra Das left for India 3/4 days after. By taking the chance of his absence the defendants created the forged deed of gift. Against the mutation made in Mutation Case No. 44/Baw/97-98 the plaintiff filed Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1998 before the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue), Patuakhali. The Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) without deciding the said miscellaneous case sent the same to the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Bawfal on 16.05.1999 for adjudication. The plaintiff felt that he would not get justice before the Assistant Commissioner (Land); so, he instituted the instant suit for cancellation of the deed of gift described in schedule 'Kha' to the plaint. 

 4. Defendant Nos. 1-4 contested the suit by filing written statement contending, inter-alia, that the plaintiff has got no cause of action to file the suit; the suit was not maintainable in its present form. Defendant Nos. 1-3 are the nephews of the Narayan Chandra Das who always used to take care of him and being impressed by their love and affection in his old age Narayan Chandra Das transferred the suit land measuring 1.48 acres to them by the deed in question. The defendants also accepted the gift. The deed of gift was executed by Narayan Chandra Das on 06.04.1985 and was registered on 29.07.1985. The plaintiff by taking chance of such delay in registering the deed of gift created the kabala dated 04.07.1985 in his favour. By threatening the defendants with dire consequences of criminal case the plaintiff took the deed of gift in his possession and subsequently did not return the same by saying that it had been lost. Being afraid of the criminal case the defendants put their signatures in the papers connected with the criminal case the statements made by the defendants in the criminal case are not correct. 

 8. From the judgment of the trial Court it appears that it decreed the suit with the finding that the suit was maintainable, there was no defect of party and was not barred by limitation. The trial Court further found that the deed of gift under challenge was not properly executed and the same was not executable in law. In coming to the said finding about the impugned deed the trial Court relied upon the fact that the defendants admitted in Complaint Case No. 9 of 1986 that the suit land was sold by Narayan Chandra Das to the plaintiff.  From the judgment of the appellate Court it appears that it dismissed the suit on the ground of limitation. The appellate Court further found that the trial Court was wrong in finding that the deed in question as forged on the admission of the defendants in criminal case. The appellate Court further found that the suit was not filed for declaration of title, but for cancellation of deed though the plaintiff allegedly acquired his right, title and possession over the suit land before execution of the deed of gift. 

 9. From the judgment of the High Court Division, it appears that the plaintiff in order to cure the defect in the frame of the suit filed an application for amendment of the plaint by adding the prayer for declaration of title which was allowed while delivering the impugned judgment. The learned Judge found some admitted facts such as, the suit land belonged to Narayan Chandra Das and the deed of sale was executed and registered by Narayan Chandra Das in favour of the plaintiff and Dilip Kumar Das. The High Court Division further found that the plaintiff alleged that after execution of the deed of transfer the suit land was handed over to him. The High Court Division further observed that regarding claim and counter claim of forgery of the deed in question no oral evidence was available with the records, the only evidence available in the record was that the defendants in the criminal case admitted that they have got no claim in the suit land and by making such admission compromised that case. The High Court Division finally concluded in favour of the plaintiff as under: 

 "Though the finding of a criminal case is not binding in a civil proceeding but the facts and circumstances of the instant case reveals that the claim of the plaintiff is proved and on proper consideration of the materials on peeped the trial Court decreed the suit but the decree passed by the trial Court was set aside by the appellate Court on the finding that the suit is barred by limitation. This finding of the appellate Court is not correct since there was no allegation that the possession of the plaintiff over the suit land had ever been threatened by anybody and before such threat he was not round to file any suit earlier on. In the facts and circumstances of the instant case I hold the view that the judgment of the trial Court is reasonable and I also hold the view that the amendment of the plaint as prayed by the plaintiff during hearing of the Rule may be allowed. Accordingly, such prayer is allowed." 

 10. We find nothing wrong with the above quoted observations and finding of the High Court Division in the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record. When the kabala executed and registered by Narayan Chandra Das transferring the suit land to the plaintiff was admitted by the contesting defendants and they also gave up their title to the suit land on the basis of the deed of gift allegedly executed by Narayan Chandra Das in a former criminal proceeding and thus, the claim of possession and there was evidence on record as to the possession of the plaintiff in the suit land we find no reason to send the suit back on remand to the trial Court simply because prayer for amendment was allowed.
